# Synthetic Chromium video references

These public clips are generated by `apps/desktop/scripts/video-parity.mjs`
from FFmpeg's `testsrc2` plus deterministic midtone and gradient expressions.
They contain no user media. The capture command runs the built desktop app
hidden, paused at 0.125, 0.625 and 1.125 seconds, using Electron 44.0.0 /
Chromium 152.0.7977.54 on macOS ARM64. Build before taking the Electron lease;
generate outside it. All operational evidence stays outside Git.

The `.rgba.zlib` data is the app's unscaled Canvas2D video source, 256×144,
top-down RGBA8. `references.json` binds its uncompressed SHA-256. These are
synthetic source rasters, not desktop screenshots. Detailed edges, gradients,
motion and midtones prevent saturated patches from hiding color conversion
errors. The fully specified BT.709 clip protects its tags; the incomplete
H.264 description proves Chromium's SD BT.601 fallback; untagged VP9 proves
Chromium's BT.709 default. HEVC10 proves the P010 upload normalization;
full-range H.264 proves the integer Canvas conversion; BT.2020 tests both
Canvas and direct texture uploads. Exposed native and Chromium YUV samples
were identical. The regression exercises all six recipes at three times and
both working precisions and requires every pixel within 1 CV, with full-range
Canvas output exact. A separate cache-switch test compares BT.2020 Canvas
and live uploads without a cache flush between readings. Some GPU half-code
rounding differs by 1; it is not described as bit exact.
